title: Orana Wildlife Park Family Review: What to Expect, Tips & Savings
meta_desc: Discover an honest family review of Orana Wildlife Park near Christchurch – age suitability, real costs, insider tips, best visiting times and how to save on tickets for a memorable day out.
intro: Orana Wildlife Park is New Zealand’s only open‑range zoo, and it promises a safari‑style experience for the whole family. Here’s what a typical day looks like with kids, plus practical advice to make the most of your visit.

sections.heading: First Impressions & Kids Experience
sections.body:
From the moment you pull into the park’s wide‑gravel carpark, the sense of adventure is palpable. The bus ride into the African Savannah feels like a mini‑safari, with giraffes, rhinos and even a pride of lions lounging just beyond the fence. Kids love the open space – they can run a short distance before the bus returns, and the occasional animal will pause to stare, sparking endless questions.

The highlight for most families is the 2 pm giraffe feeding. Little hands get to toss leaves from a safe platform, and the gentle giants bend down for a close‑up nibble. The native wildlife section offers a quieter contrast, with kiwi encounters and a walk‑through bird aviary that keeps younger children engaged.

sections.heading: Age Suitability & Value for Money
sections.body:
Orana rates itself as a 0+ destination, and that’s accurate. Toddlers will enjoy the open spaces and short bus rides, while older kids (7‑12) get more excitement from spotting predators and the interactive feeding sessions. Teens often appreciate the conservation talks and the chance to see animals they’ve only seen on TV.

At $32 per adult and $14 per child (5‑15 yrs), the price point sits in the mid‑range for NZ zoos, but the open‑range format adds value. A typical 3‑hour visit feels like a full day out, especially when you factor in the free parking and the ability to bring your own picnic.
list: Free on‑site parking (≈15‑minute drive from Christchurch city centre)

sections.heading: Insider Tips & Best Time to Visit
sections.body:
The park is busiest on school holidays and weekends, so aim for a weekday morning if you can. Arriving right at opening (9:30 am) gives you a quieter bus ride and a better chance of seeing predators active before the midday heat.

Bring a reusable water bottle – there are refill stations, but the park’s café prices are steep. Pack a snack for the kids; while you can eat in the picnic area, the only on‑site food is a fast‑food style kiosk.
list: Visit on a weekday, 9:30‑11:30 am for calm crowds
Bring a hat and sunscreen – the savannah can be bright
Pack a picnic to avoid pricey café meals

sections.heading: How to Book, Save Money & Practical Info
sections.body:
Tickets can be booked online via the Orana website – you’ll save 10 % by buying a family pass (2 adults + 2 children) for $84, compared with $92 at the gate. The website also offers occasional “early bird” discounts of up to 15 % if you purchase a month in advance.

Driving from Christchurch central takes about 20 minutes (≈15 km). If you’re staying in the city, consider a family car‑share or a rental that includes unlimited kilometres – the park’s free parking makes it a cost‑effective day trip.
list: Early‑bird discount: up to 15 % off if booked 30+ days ahead
Free on‑site parking – no extra cost for city‑based families

sections.heading: Downsides & Final Verdict
sections.body:
The open‑range layout means you spend a good portion of the day on a bus, which can be a bit long for very young children who get restless. Also, the park’s café is limited in healthy options, so you’ll need to bring your own food for picky eaters. Finally, the giraffe feeding is only at 2 pm, so if you miss that window you’ll lose one of the standout experiences.

Overall, Orana delivers a unique wildlife adventure that feels more like a safari than a traditional zoo. With a bit of planning – especially around timing and ticket purchase – it offers great value for families seeking an engaging, educational day out.
